text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games America Board Game This is a nice game if you have tons of American trivia packed away in your brain, or if you'd like lots of it. The homeschool mama part of me likes that there's educational types of facts/questions included, like when was The Star Spangled Banner written and when the United States Senate first convened. There's also tons of "bubblegum" trivia, too, though, like the debut of Gilmore Girls and questions about Simcity. Those types are more abundant.

Each card will center around 3 topics: Year, State, and Number. For example, the card labeled Orange Julius will ask what year the first restaurant opened, what state has it as the World's Fair official beverage, and how many teaspoons of sugar are in a small orange julius. With this game, you can benefit even if you don't know the answer and guess close, which is good news for me!

As far as quality goes, this is a pretty nice game. The cards look nice, and have a picture of the subject on each one. They all follow the same format, which keeps things from getting confusing, and there's a huge variety of subjects. The board is thick cardboard, and the colored pieces are wooden blocks.

Overall, this is an interesting game, and perfect for those that know lots of trivia and even those that don't and want to.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games America Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

text_fidelity_a:
Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.
text_fidelity_b: Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Grow Your Own Crystal Mini Worlds Craft and Science Kit The "Grow your own Crystal Mini Worlds" kit is a good one. It is a bit complicated compared to other craft kits of it's ilk, and requires a good amount of time, planning, and careful activation and storage of the key components, as you'll use things from project to project.

The crafts themselves are pretty impressive as well. The crystals all grew for me, which is often something that we struggle with in our home with other crystal growing kits, and the number of differnt ways your children can put them together is quite impressive. There is some modeling clay that can help with creating unique items, and there are a number of different design elements as well.

The biggest drawbacks are twofold - this requires older children, and it will definitely require more adult supervision and planning than your average arts and crafts kit, not only in terms of handling the heating, but also in aiding in the planning and reading stages of craft creation. Additionally, while I've become used to having crafting materials stored all around my home, this one takes the cake in terms of storing solutions, setting up crystal growing areas that cannot be disturbed, drying areas, and set up areas that will take over your crafting area (or in my case, the dining room) for multiple nights to multiple weeks if you make your way through projects quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Grow Your Own Crystal Mini Worlds Craft and Science Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road

Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game I am a board game afficionado. I own over 200 different strategy, social or silly games, and you'd better believe that my daughter is a gamer in waiting. Of course, as a young boy, Pretty Pretty Princess wasn't on my radar for myself, but I knew the name and the concept, and when it was my time to find a copy for my kid, there's no way I was paying the multiple hundreds for the original 80's item.

So I was thrilled when an appropriately priced remake made it's way to my house, and all it took was reading the name to hook my daughter (and interestingly, my wife as well) into a quest to become the most beautiful in all the realm.

The box for this one opens upside down for some reason, and one you get inside, you'll find a spinner, an odd, nearly blank game board, and some teeny tiny jewels to bling out your ensemble. Play is simple - you spin the spinner, attempt to move aroudn the circular board to earn all your gems, and the first one to get everything is crowned (literally) the prettiest princess.

Perhaps the most striking thing is the lack of effort they put into the board and spinner. Both are of reasonable thickness and sturdy, but there is almost nothing on the board in terms of graphic design outside of the logo on the field of white, and the spinner is literally numbers. They may have changed the font away from Times New Roman, but that's all there is to it. It looks like a high school kid's graphic design project, and not one that's going to earn high marks from the teacher.

That said, it's good to have this game back in print again, even if the game play is not particularly solid, and even if the graphics leave quite a bit to be desired. As I said, all I needed to do to get my little one to play was to tell her the name of the game, and my wife jumped right in on the nostalgia boat as well.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game

text_fidelity_a: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys Well, I'm almost at a loss for words.  I had started my review on this wonderful little squishy toy - or at least I thought it was wonderful.  I was saying how fun it was and how these squishy toys are great for stress relief (which they are), and how it kind of smelled like vanilla or egg nog.  I thought it was such a cute little doll.  And I was going to mention that I still wouldn't let pets play with it since there were some tiny excess pieces at the seams that were coming loose.  And I started looking closer at the seam that extended all the way around the middle of the toy, as I lowered one of the arms to inspect the seam where the head and arm met, that area just started coming apart.  And it only took minimal pressure for it to continue to rip.  So then I looked at the same area where the head and shoulder/arm met on the other side, and the same thing happened. It just started coming apart.  You can see what I mean in the 4th and 5th photos.  This should not happen with any squishy toy, or any other toy for that matter.  I consider this a safety concern and am giving this toy one star for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: OYEFLY Squishy Toy Soft Exquisite Horror Doll Scented Stress Relief Toy Soft Toy Kawaii Collection Slow Rising Toy Decompression SimulationToys Cure Toy for Kid Gift Toys

Power Wheels Ride-On Toy Gameday Jeep Wrangler Battery-Powered Vehicle with Sounds, Sports Net & 3 Balls, Preschool Kids Ages 3+ Years (Amazon Exclusive) This Jeep is a blast! My preschooler is a first-timer driving a motorized kid vehicle, so there was definitely a learning curve with this. I do wish it had a parent remote control to make this a little more fool-proof for first-time drivers. Even so, it is so much fun for kids to have freedom to drive around, and it’s easy to get the hang of (we’re using it on slow speed).

With that said, the assembly took quite a bit of time. There were certain parts that didn’t fit together easily, and we had to spend time pounding, readjusting the plastic pieces, and making some modifications here and there to get all of the parts to join together correctly. We made it through the process, but it wasn’t as seamless as we had anticipated. It was a 2-person job.

I will say the ball activity makes this Jeep extra entertaining, especially for sports fans, as it still offers something fun to do other than driving the car. I wish it was a little warmer outside right now so we could ride this everyday, but it’s still been a lot of fun when we get a break in the fall/winter weather. It rides just fine on a level yard, as well as on the driveway. So much fun!
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Ride-On Toy Gameday Jeep Wrangler Battery-Powered Vehicle with Sounds, Sports Net & 3 Balls, Preschool Kids Ages 3+ Years (Amazon Exclusive)

Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color This game is such a classic! I literally played the original version of Rummikub everyday in the summer at my grandma’s house growing up in the 80s & 90s. The concept of the game is simple and easy to learn (making sequences, and the joker faces can be anything you need like a wild card). I’m not sure what happened to our family’s original old set, so I’m thrilled to have a new version for our game closet.

The actual tiles have a slightly different look but do feel the same as the old ones I remember. I do miss the small circles at the bottom of each tile from the old version—they seemed easier to grab onto with that little finger spot. One thing worth mentioning is that this set doesn’t have a storage pouch for the tiles, which I think certain versions do include—this one does not, and I don’t mind at all.

This is an excellent game for kids and family game night. It’s something to get your mind thinking, strategizing, but it’s also simple and fun. I loved playing it this evening with one of my siblings, as it was like the good old days! Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color

text_fidelity_a:
All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Deluxe (EA) The special part of this particular version of Scrabble is the fact that the case is also the game. It's easy to keep everything together with this case, and it has grip-like places at the top that make toting the case around easy.

The case is hard plastic and it simply unfolds to reveal the game board, which is also plastic. The board is designed so that the tiles are placed within a square spot, and won't move around or get jarred out of place easily. Wheels are attached to the bottom(or each side of the case) to make turning the board in a circle easier. If the player wants to pull the board towards them, these wheels won't make that task easier. The wheels are turned a bit, making the board turn in a circle, not a line.

On each side of the case are drawers that pull out. These drawers are actually pretty roomy. These hold the tiles and the tile holders. The tile holders are plastic, and come within a velvet-like drawstring bag. The tiles are wooden.

Overall, this isn't the prettiest or fanciest of games. Despite being called "Deluxe", don't expect a glamorous version. It IS designed to make playing scrabble a little easier, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Deluxe (EA)

I realize the paper piece allows the grill image to be present, so I think that’s great for the flame details, but an actual plastic grate on top of the image would be much more interesting and realistic. text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover [[VIDEOID:bf921d7e8b73b1b75b44b485dab75323]] So after a week of having this unit I had 9 flights and was pleased to fly it! Although I had an issue once don't know if that was just the bird or that was me, I'm leaning toward me as I might have not turned the drone in the right direction and had a failure to calibrate or that could been just the area I was in and its inability to gain GPS, with that said it was pretty much a problem free week of flying the 270. Now dealing with the single battery was an issue, I do think they should offer a package or drone deal with 2 batteries standard. 😁.

I will say it is a great beginner drone for young teens are adults that want to get into flying. From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. The controller is smaller then what I'm used to. It felt good in the hand but a lil small for my liking as I used my Galaxy Note 9 which is the limit as far as the holder, every other feature like the FPV, follow me mode and plotting way points , and circle point of interest on a map and it's going there and coming back worked pretty well. The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover

text_fidelity_a:
Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor
